'''Debra Susan Carney''' is an American [[mathematics education|mathematics educator]], and University Distinguished Teaching Professor of mathematics, at the [[Colorado School of Mines]]. Her work focuses on educating future secondary-school mathematics teachers.{{r|relevant}}

==Education and career==
Carney majored in mathematics at the [[University of Vermont]], graduating in 1991.{{r|profile}} She completed a Ph.D. in [[mathematical logic]] in 1998 at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]].{{r|flipped}} Her dissertation, ''Linear Structures with Few Substructures'', was supervised by Michael C. Laskowski.{{r|mg}}

After both completing doctorates in mathematics at the University of Maryland, she and her husband Nic Ormes became faculty members at the [[University of Denver]], where her husband still teaches. In 2012, after nine years at the university, Carney moved to her present position at the Colorado School of Mines.{{r|flipped}} She was named University Distinguished Teaching Professor for 2023–2024.{{r|distinguished}}

==Recognition==
In 2022, Carney was named a Fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], "for her extraordinary support of women in the mathematical sciences through personal mentorship and leadership of her local AWM chapter; and for community outreach activities that have had lasting and positive impacts on the lives of women and girls ranging from high school students to faculty members".{{r|fawm}}
